sources.citation: Survey of Dialects of the Marathi Language (SDML), Deccan College Pune & Rajya Marathi Vikas Sanstha, 2017- (sdml.ac.in): features, narrations, previous-projects pages
sources.note: Online output is lexical and grammatical feature maps only; Palghar/Thane narrations not published; confirms Ghatage's Survey of Marathi Dialects (1963-76: Konkani of S. Kanara, Kudali, Kunbi of Mahad, Cochin, Konkani of Kankon, Varli of Thana, Marathi of Kasargod, Gawdi, Bhili of Dangs) has no Vadval/Phudagi volume.

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. 1905. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. VII: Indo-Aryan Family, Southern Group: Specimens of the Marathi Language. Calcutta: Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing. Vad'val pp. 144-147, Phud'gi p. 148, Samvedi pp. 148 ff. (archive.org;ernet.dli.2015.32107, scanned text)
sources.note: Silent for Phudagi/Vadval. Phud'gi (p. 148) is one paragraph: a Standard Words and Phrases list was received, dialect 'almost identical with Vad'val'. Vad'val sketch (p. 144) lists segmental traits (cerebral d kept, n for cerebral n, ch > s, s/sh > h, h-dropping) and morphology; no accent/stress statement. The volume's only accent statements are for Konkani (p. 167 'The accent usually rests on the final syllable..') and Standard Marathi schwa-deletion rules (pp. 20-21), not applicable to this variety.

sources.citation: English Wikipedia 'Phudagi language' and Marathi Wikipedia pages 'वाडवळी भाषा', 'मराठीतील बोलीभाषा', 'पाचकळशी', 'ख्रिस्ती वाडवळ समाज', 'सामवेदी बोली'
sources.note: Nothing on stress; identify Phudagi with Vadvali (Vasai/Palghar, Panchkalshi & Chaukalshi communities); Samvedi page names Naresh Naik's Marathi monograph on the adjacent Samvedi dialect.

sources.citation: Devy, G. N. & Arun Jakhade (eds.). 2017. The Languages of Maharashtra. People's Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. 17 (Parts 1-2). sources.citation: Naik, Naresh. [ca. 2016-2017]. Samvedi boli: sanrachna ani svarup [The Samvedi dialect: structure and form]. (Marathi; Virar; awarded K. M. Ujalambkar and N. G. Kalelkar prizes 2018, per Marathi Wikipedia)

sources.note: Book-length Marathi description of the immediately adjacent and closely similar Samvedi dialect of Vasai (LSI groups Vad'val, Phud'gi, Samvedi together); a 'sanrachna' (structure) monograph is the likeliest place for a svaraghat/balaghat (stress) paragraph in this dialect cluster; may also treat Vadvali comparatively. Exact year/publisher not verified.
